outcomes: Each packwerk pack and local gem of a Ruby repository is a Putnami project, with an edge to each pack its package.yml lists and each local gem its Gemfile or gemspec names, and the probe answers the application the same way

putnami lint runs RuboCop in each component, and putnami test runs RSpec or Rails's Minitest runner on each component from the directory of its Gemfile; a second run over an unchanged tree is a cache hit
The test task reads the JUnit report and the SimpleCov Cobertura report into the test and coverage summary of the component, with only the lines of its own files
A component overrides any value of the Ruby profile in its putnami.json, and the override reaches the cache key
putnami install runs bundle install at each stack root, and lint and test install a stack root whose bundle is incomplete first, so a fresh checkout needs no bundle install by hand

On a machine with no Ruby, or none the repository's .ruby-version or .tool-versions accepts, putnami install then putnami lint and test work with a Ruby the extension pins, and a workspace without @putnami/ruby or without a Ruby component downloads none
putnami install fetches and installs the bundle of each stack root, serve and run start an application, and package and publish produce its OCI image with no Docker daemon
nonGoals: Building or publishing Ruby archives, downloading Bundler on its own, and installing RuboCop, RSpec or a gem outside the bundle: the pinned Ruby comes from the rv-ruby release archives, its Bundler is the one it ships or the one bundle install switches to, and the tools come from the repository's own bundle
A build task: Ruby has no compile step, and a gem reaches its registry through gem push; package builds the image of an application only
Reading the constant references packwerk check reads
gems.rb and gems.locked, the other names Bundler accepts
A project for the application at the workspace root, which the CLI does not discover yet
A workspace-fetch: Bundler downloads a gem only as it installs it, and bundle cache writes vendor/cache into the repository
JRuby and TruffleRuby, whose --version the toolchain check does not read
Packaging an image on a host of another OS or architecture than the image's: the bundle's native extensions build on the host, so a team packages on a Linux runner of the target architecture

requirements.text: The probe answers, for each candidate directory the observe Ruby detector knows as a component: its gem name, else its pack path, else the workspace directory's name, the directories of the components it depends on, the extension @putnami/ruby, the tag ruby, and metadata naming its stack root, the nearest of its own directory and the workspace root that holds a Gemfile, and the expected Ruby and Bundler versions.

Each task first compares ruby --version with .ruby-version or .tool-versions, in the component then at its stack root: a mismatch fails with stacks.toolchain_mismatch unless check is warn. A bundle --version other than the BUNDLED WITH of Gemfile.lock warns with the same code, because the core checks before the install step that fixes it. Lint then runs bundle exec rubocop in the component; test runs from the stack root on the component's test directory.

The probe names each component's profile variant: rspec when it holds a spec/**/*_spec.rb file, which runs bundle exec rspec on its spec directory with the RspecJunitFormatter; minitest when it holds a test/**/*_test.rb file and no spec file, which runs bundle exec rails test on its test directory; untested when it holds no Ruby file under spec/ or test/, whose test runs nothing and passes; rspec otherwise. Such a file is a workspace input, so it changes the variant and the key.

The test task reads its JUnit report and the SimpleCov Cobertura report at the stack root's coverage/coverage.xml through the evidence readers. The coverage summary counts only the files under the component's directory outside a nested component; a covered file in no component is the warning stacks.coverage_unmapped. A failed case fails the task with stacks.test_failed, and a missing report with stacks.report_missing.

The ruby:lint selector answers the files RuboCop inspects by default and the RuboCop configuration, outside vendor, node_modules and tmp, and not the test fixtures, .rspec or the ERB views: a change to one of them reruns test and keeps the lint key.

options["@putnami/ruby"] in a component's own putnami.json overrides the profile after its variant: an object merges, null removes the member, and any other value replaces the profile's whole. The steps run and the files the ruby:<task> selectors answer follow the resolved profile, and putnami.json is an input of every task. An unknown member fails the task with stacks.project_config_invalid.

The manifest passes the stack core's conformance kit: its markers are the profile's, it lists the ruby:lint and ruby:test selectors, and each command runs one task that depends on the same task upstream, reads its selector and the profile's stack-root files for that task, and declares its command-output reports directory.

Before lint and test, the install step runs bundle check at the component's stack root with the selected Ruby, then bundle install when the bundle is incomplete or bundle --version is not the BUNDLED WITH of Gemfile.lock, one run per root at a time; bundle install then switches to the locked Bundler. Offline, it runs bundle install --local, from the gems on the machine and in the gem cache workspace-fetch fills, and a Bundler mismatch alone installs nothing.

workspace-install runs bundle install at each stack root of the workspace's projects, except a project disable.tags excludes and a root whose bundle check passes with the Bundler its Gemfile.lock states, which the force flag installs again. A run with offline dependencies runs bundle install --local, which reads the gem cache workspace-fetch fills. With no Ruby it warns and passes.
deps-upgrade runs bundle update at each stack root of the workspace's projects, with the Ruby the toolchain check selects.
lint checks every relative link and anchor of the component's README.md files and doc/ trees, and a broken one fails it, unless the docs-links flag is false. The check needs neither Ruby nor Bundler.

test with the test flag, short -t, passes its value to RSpec as -e and to rails test as -n with the value quoted as a regular expression, so a component in which it selects no test passes. The value is part of the task's key, so a filtered result never answers an unfiltered run.

When the workspace holds a Ruby component, toolchain-resolve answers ruby with a shipped release: a stable 3.2, 3.3, 3.4 or 4.0 patch of a fixed rv-ruby release, with an archive and a SHA-256 per platform. It picks among the releases every component accepts, else those the root accepts: a committed accepted pin, else the highest. With no Ruby component, no accepted release, or no archive for the platform, such as Windows, it answers no pin.

Each task runs the ruby on PATH when its version satisfies the stated version. When ruby is missing, or outside the statement, the task puts the Ruby the workspace lock pins first on PATH, so its bundle runs too, and repeats the check. A project whose toolchain.check is warn keeps the ruby on PATH. With no pinned Ruby installed, the check fails as it did before.

workspace-fetch runs bundle cache at each stack root with a Gemfile.lock, with no install, a frozen lockfile, a private install path and a private local configuration, so it downloads the locked gems into the extension's gem cache, runs none of their code and writes nothing in the repository. It never prunes the cache, which every root shares. A stack root with no Gemfile.lock is skipped. With no Ruby it warns and passes.

serve runs bundle exec rails server -b 0.0.0.0 when the application holds bin/rails, else bundle exec rackup -o 0.0.0.0, with the port flag, default 3000 and 0 for a free port, in the directory of an application after the toolchain check and the install step, with PORT set, and emits a ready event once the server accepts connections. An application is a component whose directory holds config.ru; a library is skipped.

run executes bundle exec ruby with the entrypoint flag, default bin/rails, in the directory of an application after the toolchain check and the install step, passes it the words of the args flag, and exits with its exit code. A library is skipped.

package assembles an OCI image of an application without Docker: its production bundle under /usr/local/bundle, its files under /app without tests, run output and secrets, and tmp/ and log/ owned by its non-root user, on the digest-pinned ruby:<version>-slim-trixie of the host Ruby's minor or a named base, which fails with ruby.base_not_pinned without a digest. It runs rails server or rackup on PORT 8080 in production. Two packagings of one tree on a machine give the same image. A library packages nothing.

package fails with ruby.package_host_mismatch, before it installs anything, when the packaging host is not a glibc Linux machine whose CPU is the architecture of the platform flag, default linux/amd64; the message names the host and the target and says to package on a Linux runner of the target architecture.

publish with the docker channel pushes the packaged image to registries.oci.publish, or to the docker-registry flag, through the shared publisher, and reports it as a release-set member. A library publishes nothing.
